newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Police fire tear gas in Taiwan youth prison riot.
newsitem.headline: Police fire tear gas in Taiwan youth prison riot.

text.p: Inmates at a juvenile detention centre torched their cells, smashed a workshop and briefly held a supervisor hostage, prompting police to fire blanks and tear gas in Taiwan's worst prison violence in 14 years.

Detainees were still shouting and banging on bars Wednesday morning as the melee that began Tuesday lingered despite the transfer of 90 inmates to another centre, wardens said by telephone from the facility in northern Hsinchu city.

The rioters, all young offenders apparently unhappy about working conditions and parole requirements, used sticks and steel bars to smash up the electronics workshop, according to state-run television reports.
They seized a supervisor but soon released him.
"He suffered fractures and a mild concussion but is in stable condition," the television said of the official.
One juvenile was injured slightly while trying to protect the supervisor from fellow inmates, witnesses said.
State-run television said more than 700 police were deployed at the scene and showed them firing blanks and tear gas. Police used three fire trucks to extinguish small fires ignited in the cells.
About 300 police were still standing guard outside the centre as of Wednesday afternoon.
Prison officials said they had launched an investigation to find the cause of the riot.
A Hsinchu lawmaker who entered the facility on Tuesday night said the detainees complained their working hours were too long and requirements for parole too stringent.
"I told them that as their legislator I would relay their messages," Hsinchu parliament deputy Lin Cheng-tseh said.
"Everything seemed calmer when I left, but when I went back (later)...the police were saying they wanted to use tear gas."
The prison violence was Taiwan's worst since 1982, when two riots hit the same Hsinchu compound.
